absorptions.semantic_mapping: Hepta's session-owned refresh lock serializes every rebuild/publication cycle, while its desired/applied generation state retains the exact pending intent until a matching manager generation publishes. Cancellation, invalid configuration, or supersession therefore cannot consume the desired refresh, and stale generations cannot replace the published manager. This is a richer generation-bound equivalent of the upstream pending-bit plus gate behavior during the active session lifetime.

behavioral_evidence.assertion: Each consumed explicit refresh rebuilds configured MCP connections.
Cancellation cannot consume the pending desired generation before publication.
Concurrent desired generations publish only the latest valid replacement.
A catalog entry cannot dispatch through a different published manager generation.

non_claims: No byte-for-byte or type-level equivalence with upstream McpRefresh is claimed.
The local coordinator remains a generation state plus session-owned lock rather than one closeable semaphore abstraction.
This narrow equivalence does not close R6 authentication-generation refresh or background prewarm.

deferrals.reason: The upstream abstraction explicitly closes a semaphore during shutdown and places pending invalidation plus gate ownership in one module. Hepta currently relies on session/task teardown and keeps the generation state and serialization lock as adjacent Session fields. Consolidating those fields while R6 authentication publication is changing would add churn without closing a current behavioral defect.
missing_prerequisites: explicit local shutdown behavior for a refresh waiting on the publication lock
one coordinator API that preserves desired and applied generations
regression proof that structural consolidation does not weaken same-generation catalog and client binding
non_claims: The upstream closeable refresh semaphore was not copied.
No claim is made that task teardown is identical to explicit gate closure.
